To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

organizational trust, socialization, and sensitivity to privacy are the most significant factors influencing the level of trust an individual places on an HRIS technology (i.e., technology trust), and that the level of technology trust is the most significant factor influencing the success of an organization’s HRIS implementation process.
organizational trust, socialization, and predisposition are the most important factors in determining technology trust.

organizational trust, socialization, and technology adoption influence an individual’s technology trust, and that technology trust, organizational community, and organizational culture influence an HRIS implementation success.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the antecedents of trust in HRIS technology and its relationship to HRIS success.
the role technology trust plays in the implementation of HRIS.
how the trust that an individual places in a technology (technology trust), as opposed to an individual or organization (organizational trust), influences HRIS implementation success.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the level of trust in an HRIS technology (i.e., the technology trust) will be influenced by the level of organizational trust, pooled-interdependence, organizational culture, organizational community, technology adoption, socialization, and sensitivity to privacy.
technology trust is a key determinant in the success or failure of an HRIS.
technology trust is a critical factor in HRIS implementation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
technology trust is influenced by organizational trust, organizational culture, and the HRIS technology itself.
the HRIS implementation success will be enhanced when the technology is trusted and when the technology trust is high.
trust is a complex construct that can be viewed from a variety of different perspectives.
The main takeaway from our work is that
trust is not a simple, single, or static construct.
HRIS implementation success is influenced by the degree of technology trust that individuals place in the HRIS.
HR professionals need to be aware of the importance of technology trust in the implementation of HRIS.
